messages.subject: What variety
messages.text:
I would appreciate maps showing which varieties are native to what areas of the country. I live in Albuquerque, New Mexico. This is a high desert. We get below freezing temperatures in the winter and above 100° in the summer. It is very dry. There is very little rainfall or snow.
 If I am going to plant milkweed, and I want to, I want it to be the ACTUAL variety that lives in New Mexico. How do I know that?

messages.subject: Re: What variety
messages.text:
Hi,
 

 Sorry for the very long delay. Probably too late, but just in case:

For Albuquerque and the New Mexico high desert, the species most native to your region would be Asclepias fascicularis (Narrowleaf milkweed) and Asclepias asperula, though availability varies. Of the species we currently carry, Asclepias fascicularis is available and is one of the better fits for dry, hot climates with cold winters.

For the most precise answer on what's truly native to your specific area, the USDA Plants Database (plants.usda.gov) lets you search by state and species, which would give you a definitive map. The Xerces Society also has excellent regional guides for pollinator plants in the Southwest.

You can see what we have in stock here: https://lasclay.com/en-us/products/milkweed-seeds

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
